terms.comment: Classically inclīnāre is to bend or lower; with sē, of a bow in worship, it is the Vulgate’s (Inclīnāvit sē homō, et adōrāvit Dominum). To bow the head is caput inclīnāre. In the Orthodox churches the bow from the waist with the sign of the cross (Greek μετάνοια) and the full prostration to the ground are regular parts of prayer; in the Latin rite the bow of the head or body and the genuflection are the usual signs.

terms.gloss: worship, do reverence (with a bow or prostration)
evidence: Ov. Met. 3.18: Phoebum taciturnus adōrat (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Worship shown in a gesture, Greek προσκυνεῖν: in Rome a hand to the lips and a turn of the whole body, under the emperors a prostration (prōcumbēns, Suet. Vit. 2; Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: bow down to the ground, prostrate oneself
evidence: Caes. BG 7.15: prōcumbunt Gallīs omnibus ad pedēs Biturigēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The full prostration: to fall forward to the ground, as suppliants did.

phrases.latin: Inclīnāvit sē homō, et adōrāvit Dominum
phrases.english: The man bowed and worshipped the Lord
and they fell down and worshipped him (the Magi)
